dedupe_keys.name: the jacchia bowman 2008 empirical thermospheric density model

description: JB2008 estimates thermospheric density using solar and geomagnetic proxies. It revises earlier Jacchia-Bowman formulations with temperature and seasonal-density terms for satellite-drag analysis. The resource is documented by NASA Community Coordinated Modeling Center (metadata publisher; developer not specified). The documented physical domain is Thermosphere; grid spacing, supported periods and cadence depend on this version and its chosen configuration. The documentation links Runs-on-Request, Public Repository. A software licence and any external distribution charge are not stated. The source describes an empirical atmosphere model; it does not establish accuracy for every orbit or storm. The documented space-weather effects make it a potential environmental input for infrastructure hazard exposure and resilience simulations. It is related to platform-nasa-ccmc in this catalogue. Spatial and temporal resolution were not independently established.

inputs: JB2008 requires solar inputs [F10.7, S10.7 (EUV), M10.7 (FUV), Y10.7 (X-ray and Lyman-α) indices, the centered 81-day average of the four indices] and geomagnetic inputs [Ap and Dst indices]
